If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid overestimation.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early-horizon (days 1–5) to compensate for downward bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–3% for late-horizon (days 21–30) to correct for momentum reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for mid-horizon to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for early-horizon to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >2% from true path, apply linear correction: subtract 0.2% per 1.5 sentiment cycle shift.
